content:
oli: heads up onboarding Nebula-2.5B (fp16 -> int8-awq) — generation quality looks fine short-form but long-context summarization has strange repetition + topic drift starting ~3k tokens.
sara: paste the eval numbers + conversion command please.
ben: also which awq version and whether you used per-channel?
oli: eval: `rouge_l_fp16=39.8, rouge_l_int8=36.0` command: `python convert.py --model nebula-2.5b --to int8 --backend awq --per-channel`
export-bot: CI: models/nebula25b-int8  4 failed tests, 10 passed  logs at /ci/models/6109876543/logs
anya: quick suspicion: some AWQ converter paths cast rotary sin/cos precompute into fp16 before quant scaling which can warp angular values when downstream kernels expect float32-derived angles. Did you check rotary_base and any "rotary_precision" metadata?
oli: I didn't. artifact config: {"n_heads":20,"head_dim":64,"rotary_emb":true,"rotary_base":8192,"rotary_precision":"fp16","head_order":"standard"}
sara: original hub config?
oli: hub: {"n_heads":20,"head_dim":64,"rotary_emb":true,"rotary_base":8192,"rotary_precision":"fp32","head_order":"standard"}
ben: there we go. converter set rotary_precision to fp16. If the runtime precomputes sin/cos in fp16 for long sequences, rounding error accumulates in the streaming path and can destabilize autoregression, especially with long-prefix caching.
anya: also check whether converter fused rotary into the attention kernels (common for perf presets). If fusion assumed fp32 angles but got fp16, mismatch.
oli: converter snippet: `python convert.py --model nebula-2.5b --preset perf-compact --backend awq --per-channel` I guess perf-compact enabled fp16 rotary for speed.
sara: plan: (1) re-convert with `--preserve-rotary-precision=fp32` and disable rotary fusion; (2) dump logits for deterministic prompt for 512 vs 4096 tokens and compute per-token KL and L2 against fp16 baseline; (3) add unit in converter e2e that asserts rotary_precision preserved or is explicitly documented.
ben: also test AWQ older patch where asymmetric scaling of rotary projections happened (I recall a bug where row-wise scales didn't apply to rotary matrices). Run weight-slice dequant checks: dequantized_w ≈ fp32_w within tol. Pseudocode: `for slice in proj_slices: assert np.allclose(deq(slice), fp(slice), atol=1e-2)`
oli: kicking rerun with flags: `--preserve-rotary-precision=fp32 --disable-rotary-fusion --tokenizer=embedded` now.
export-bot: Job queued: models/nebula25b-int8-rerun (#6109876543-rerun)
sara: if rerun recovers, add a test in the perf preset docs and logger warning when rotary_precision is downgraded.
ben: and add a long-context parity test for streaming kernels to CI, so FP32 vs FP16 rotary differences show up early.
export-bot: Rerun finished: 0 failed, 13 passed  artifacts at /ci/models/6109876640/results
oli: rerun eval: `rouge_l_fp16=39.8, rouge_l_int8-preserve=39.4`  nearly fixed. root cause = perf-compact preset forced fp16 rotary and fusion.
anya: nice. Actions: (A) add converter assert for rotary_precision and a warning in perf presets; (B) add dequant slice L2 check into export CI; (C) add streaming long-context rotary parity tests. I'll file PRs for (A)+(C).
sara: thanks. i'll add (B) to the AWQ test checklist.
oli: thanks everyone  closing the onboarding ticket and noting preset caveat in the model doc. :white_check_mark:
